scope: Independent code/maintainability reviews; NOT owner merge approval or hosted CI acceptance

maintainability.disposition: Accepted. Preparation is separated into CLI consent, credential-free downloads, private filesystem/process boundaries, per-tool installers, and read-only inspection. The verifier reuses the inspection API rather than duplicating its integrity/freshness rules. Shared staging and archive helpers serve concrete repeated behavior; per-tool installation remains explicit without an unnecessary plugin framework. Workflow checks intentionally freeze reviewed trust-boundary settings, while tool/platform locks and the Cargo license policy retain distinct responsibilities. Independent AST/nonblank measurements found no 300-line file or 50-line function triggers in the owned Python scope: the largest production file is scripts/tooling/install.py at 108 nonblank lines, the largest production function is verify_database at 35, and the largest test function is the container contract at 46. No scope-expanding abstractions, god files, or required refactoring identified.

core_initial_findings.title: The required Rust integration gate passes when the integration suite is absent
QML lifecycle hooks can make an entirely empty native suite pass
Standalone Rust verification does not detect drift in the advertised Rust version declarations

core_architecture_disposition.disposition: Accepted after the three logic-gate corrections passed independent re-review; the prior responsibility/maintainability assessment required no size-driven restructuring.

hotspots.kind: reviewed qualitative hotspot, not a threshold violation
hotspots.disposition: Accepted: the nesting is concentrated in descriptor-relative filesystem classification, exclusion/error accounting and language dispatch. Lexical parsing is already separated into metrics_lexical.py. These responsibilities share the coverage contract; further splitting is not justified merely to lower a metric.

Accepted: snapshotting, the environment allowlist and bounded child execution belong to the verification boundary, with Docker-specific construction/cleanup extracted separately. Timeout/output-overflow tests actually execute subprocesses inside the canonical outer boundary.

Accepted: related public-report, parser, scope, threshold and no-follow traversal cases use compact generated fixtures. The suite contains a rationale and does not exceed the 300-nonblank-line trigger.

metrics.qualification: These are the repository reporter's defined nonblank/control metrics, not independent cyclomatic complexity, coupling, duplication or API measurements. Python uses AST spans; Rust/QML are explicitly lexical approximations. Generated, frozen and legacy exclusions and test partitioning are disclosed.

architectural_review: Rust exposes a narrow pure interpret function, two small enums and static help; the executable alone owns argument collection, output and exit status. Typed value-free diagnostics, forbidden unsafe code, bounded argument collection and explicit unsupported modes keep #8-#10 responsibilities out of this foundation.

Rust integration fixtures centralize environment clearing, private synthetic tree setup, before/after comparisons and RAII cleanup. They do not pretend to detect arbitrary host writes; the documentation correctly assigns that protection to the outer verifier.
QML contains only a native toolchain sentinel, no durable business state, daemon/app model or speculative bridge. The dependency-free package and absence of future scaffolding are appropriate to #7.

Verification direction is entrypoint -> check inventory/runner -> isolated subprocess boundary; Docker construction and native QML adaptation are separate. Online preparation is not imported as a runtime dependency of the product CLI.

Metrics file traversal/report policy and lexical parsing are separated on a substantive responsibility boundary. Approximation limits are unusually explicit, and regression tests exercise malformed source, no-follow handling, scope partitioning and strict advisory thresholds.

The cross-file Rust pin relationship and suite-specific execution evidence are duplicated assumptions rather than enforced shared rules; address these narrowly through CORE-1 through CORE-3 instead of adding broad abstractions or unrelated refactoring.

maintainability.disposition: Accepted scoped fixes. Existing broader maintainability and tools/CI reviews remain applicable to unchanged code; no unrelated refactor or scope extension is required.
observations: checks.py retains a single shared inventory and result validator; explicit cli integration-target selection is appropriately narrow for the current single-package workspace.
The QML change adds positive native test-function evidence while preserving zero-failure, zero-skip and zero-blacklist requirements; it does not infer execution from lifecycle-inclusive totals.

preflight.py is a small cohesive adapter that reuses tooling.inspection.verify_existing rather than duplicating executable integrity, version or advisory inspection. It adds only the declared exact Rust-version relationship.

The regression fixtures are focused, use private temporary copies, and run real Cargo and tool inspection inside the canonical offline boundary. TOOLCHAIN.md accurately distinguishes the pinned workspace release from a separately qualified lower MSRV.

fix_recheck.summary: PASS: independent bounded re-review and actual isolated execution confirm CORE-1, CORE-2 and CORE-3 are fixed; the canonical gate passes, absent/empty integration and lifecycle-only/skipped/failed QML suites fail closed, and Rust declaration or compiler-pin drift fails preflight and blocks subsequent required checks.

independent_fault_results.observed: Cargo rejects the missing explicit cli target.
Cargo reports zero integration tests; successful library execution cannot satisfy this target.
Two empty native TestCases report four lifecycle passes and no test_* PASS; rejected.
A real passing test_* function plus one skipped function is rejected.
A real passing test_* function plus one failed function is rejected.
A PASS test_* line plus a nonzero blacklist total is rejected; this specific case is a parser fixture, not a native blacklist execution.
